findings.claim:
The correction put a literal backslash-n into the no-JavaScript starter. Line 486 of the reading version's <pre><code> now reads '    // 1. Give each constant its value in cents:
    //    1, 5, 10, 25.' as one line. With JavaScript disabled at 570 px this <pre> is visible (white-space: pre-wrap), so the learner sees the characters '
' inside a Java comment. Beginners have just met 
 as an escape sequence in strings, so this looks like code they should type. It also no longer matches the editor starter, where comment 1 is two lines. The other four rewrapped pages have no such stray text: their no-JavaScript starters equal the PEP_PAGE starters exactly.
findings.recommendation: Replace the literal '\n' with a real line break so the no-JavaScript starter equals the PEP_PAGE starter, then regenerate artifact.md if it changes.

findings.claim: The correction rewrapped the Activity 3 starter comments in PEP_PAGE and in the no-JavaScript <pre>, but the fieldset's data-static-alt reading text still carries the old line breaks, for example '// 5. Add a method String label() that returns switch (this) // with one case per constant and no default.'. artifact.md copies that text into '### explore', so the companion keeps the pre-correction comment breaks. The words are the same and the text is flattened onto one line, so a reader loses nothing; it is a stale copy, not a teaching error.
findings.recommendation: Regenerate or edit data-static-alt so its starter matches the new comment breaks, then regenerate artifact.md.
